title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 5th District
area: Eastern Kentucky and Appalachia, including London, Hazard and Middlesboro.

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and Ned Pillersdorf advanced without opposition.

candidates.name: Hal Rogers
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, defeating Kevin Smith, Benjamin Hurley, Brandon Monhollen and Jerry Shelton.

summary.text: Hal Rogers is the Republican incumbent for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District, which he has represented since 1981. An attorney from Pulaski County who was born in rural Kentucky, he became Dean of the U.S. House in 2022 and chaired the House Appropriations Committee from 2011 to 2016. He currently chairs the Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies.

background.text: Born December 31, 1937, in Barrier, Kentucky, and attended Wayne County High School in Monticello, Kentucky.
Attended Western Kentucky University from 1956 to 1957, then earned an A.B. (1962) and an LL.B. (1964) from the University of Kentucky.
Served in the Kentucky and North Carolina Army National Guard from 1956 to 1963.
Worked as an attorney in Kentucky's Pulaski and Rockcastle counties before his political career.

Has represented Kentucky's 5th District since 1981. On September 2, 2021, he became the longest-serving member of Congress from Kentucky, and on March 18, 2022, he became Dean of the U.S. House as its longest-serving member.

Chaired the House Appropriations Committee from 2011 through 2016. According to his official biography, he was chosen in 2003 to lead the first Homeland Security Subcommittee and has chaired or been ranking member of six Appropriations subcommittees.
In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he sits on the Appropriations Committee, including its Defense subcommittee, and chairs the Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies subcommittee.

His official biography credits him with helping found regional economic development and anti-drug organizations including Operation UNITE, Southeast Kentucky Economic Development (SKED), the Center for Rural Development, Eastern Kentucky PRIDE and Shaping Our Appalachian Region (SOAR).

priorities.text: Says he supports federal resources for rural health care, including Community Health Centers and the Center of Excellence in Rural Health in Hazard, and continued efforts to combat prescription-drug and opioid abuse in the region.
Says he supports "an all of the above, market-based approach to energy policy," including continued coal mining, to keep electricity costs low for the district.

positions.summary: Voted for the Secure America Act, which provides funding for ICE and Border Patrol through September 2029, including $38 billion for ICE personnel and removal operations.
positions.quote: Congressman Rogers voted for the reconciliation package to provide long-term funding for ICE and Border Patrol through September 2029.

positions.summary: Voted for the SAVE America Act, which his office describes as requiring proof of American citizenship for federal voter registration.
positions.quote: The bill requires proof of American citizenship for federal voter registration to restore election integrity and prevent foreign interference.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and chairs its Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies (119th Congress, 2025-2026).
Chaired the Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science in the 118th Congress (2023-2024); previously chaired the full Appropriations Committee (2011-2016).
Founded Operation UNITE, a regional anti-drug initiative combining investigations, treatment, and education, and helped establish a national grant program for Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs.

candidates.name: Ned Pillersdorf
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without opposition after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Ned Pillersdorf is the Democratic nominee for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District, a Prestonsburg attorney who has practiced law in Floyd County for more than 40 years. He says he has run a "poverty volume" law practice and been involved with several nonprofits. He is running against incumbent Hal Rogers, citing opposition to cuts to Medicaid, Medicare and food stamps and Rogers's vote for the 2025 reconciliation tax law.

background.text: Is a Prestonsburg attorney who, according to WYMT, has worked in his law office and in several nonprofits in the Floyd County area for more than 40 years.
Says he has had an "underdog/poverty volume" law practice for 44 years and has been involved with several nonprofits.
Announced his candidacy for Congress on July 4, 2025, after saying he would run against Rogers over the 2025 reconciliation bill.
The Democratic primary for the seat on May 19, 2026, was canceled, and he advanced to the general election as the Democratic nominee.

priorities.text: "If you support the ongoing proposed slashing of: Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps, funds to help low income folks pay their utilities, and the defunding of public television, public radio, job corp, cancer research, etc – all so the billionaire class can get a deficit busting tax break – I don't expect to persuade you to support my candidacy."

"I intend to campaign on rural issues that include the expansion of healthcare access, the expansion of better internet access, expansion of educational opportunities, and to finally do something about the lack of cleaning drinking water in many of our communities."

statements.quote: I won’t stop fighting until every resident of the 5th District gets the coverage and care they deserve.
statements.context: Press release on the 60th anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid, July 30, 2025

statements.quote: Instead they insist that giving another round of massive tax breaks to the billionaire class will solve all of our problems.
statements.context: Press release on filing his candidacy, Nov. 13, 2025

summary.text: Gerardo Serrano is an independent candidate for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District. A small-business owner and farmer who was born in Chicago, he has lived in the district for over 25 years and says he became active in politics after experiencing civil asset forfeiture. He previously ran in Republican primaries against Hal Rogers and campaigns as independent of both major parties, focused on constitutional rights and due process.

background.text: Says he was born in Chicago and has lived in Kentucky's 5th District for over 25 years.
Says his first job was at an A&P grocery store for about three years, and describes himself as a small-business owner and farmer.
Says he became involved in politics after experiencing civil asset forfeiture firsthand.
Ran against Hal Rogers in the Republican primary in 2020 (8.9% of the vote) and in 2022 (5.9%); Rogers won both. He is on the 2026 ballot as an independent.

priorities.text: "I am independent—not controlled by either political party, political insiders, or special interests. I will answer to the people of Kentucky's 5th District, demand transparency, oppose wasteful omnibus bills, and insist that Congress vote on major issues openly and individually."

"Our children should not have to leave Eastern Kentucky to build a future. I want to attract businesses, create good jobs, strengthen infrastructure, and make this district a place where families can prosper."
"In Congress, I will fight civil asset forfeiture so the government cannot take your property without first proving you committed a crime."

positions.summary: Campaign website says Congress, not one president, must decide whether America goes to war; his survey lists requiring Congress to vote before sending Americans into war.
positions.quote: Congress—not a militia and not one president—must decide whether America goes to war.

statements.quote: I will support stronger border enforcement, faster lawful immigration, and firm action against cartels and traffickers—while protecting due process and America’s constitutional principles.
statements.context: On his campaign website ("Border Security Is National Security")

summary.text: Mikel Wein is an independent candidate for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District from Letcher County. He describes a first job as a contract archaeologist and says he has spent recent months knocking on doors across the district. He campaigns on ending corporate control of Eastern Kentucky's land and energy resources, a national healthcare system, and reducing U.S. military spending abroad.

background.text: Says he lives in a log cabin in Letcher County on land that has been in his family for over a century.
Says his first job was as a contract archaeologist, working at Fort Lee for about a year.
Says he spent the months before the election knocking on doors and listening to residents across the 5th District. He is on the 2026 ballot as an independent.

priorities.text: "Eastern KY deserves to end the decades of corporate and monopoly control of its land, energy, and natural wealth, and chart its own future."

positions.summary: Supports a national healthcare system that prioritizes people over profit.
positions.quote: a national healthcare system that prioritizes people over profit

positions.summary: Says he supports halting U.S. military support for other countries, including Israel, over allegations of human rights abuses.
positions.quote: halt military support for other countries, such as Israel, that commit genocide or other crimes against humanity

positions.summary: Says he supports defunding ICE, describing its activities as unlawfully harming people.
positions.quote: de-fund services, such as ICE, that are unlawfully harming people in our own country and making us afraid.

summary.text: Billy Ray Wilson is an independent write-in candidate for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District. His campaign website says he would propose constitutional amendments if elected; no other issue statements or biographical profile were found.

priorities.text: "I will submit Constitutional Amendments to bring the US Constitution up to date for the future."
"Other amendments will address immigration, socialism, religious abuse, and foreign policy."

researchNotes: Rogers's federal key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script; his vote on the 2025 reconciliation bill is included here only as characterized by his opponent's campaign, since the official roll call was not independently checked. Checked Rogers's official issues pages (appropriations, economic development, education, energy, environment, homeland security, health care, illegal drugs, taxes, tourism, transportation, veterans) and immigration services page; no statements found there addressing abortion, guns, immigration enforcement specifically, rent regulation, housing supply, climate transition pace, police funding, school choice, congestion pricing, minimum wage, Israel aid, or tariffs. No public information beyond his name on the ballot was found for write-in candidate Billy Ray Wilson. Update: Pillersdorf's positions come from his campaign press releases (no Ballotpedia survey; no abortion, guns, climate or minimum-wage statements found). Serrano's earlier guns entry was moved to a statement because "defend the Second Amendment" does not address stricter gun laws. Wilson (write-in) has a personal campaign blog with one statement on presidential war powers; his other posts are on religion and history and were not used. Biographies for Pillersdorf, Serrano and Wein rely on their own statements and a local news report; no further independent biographical coverage was found, and none was found for write-in candidate Billy Ray Wilson.
